q: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of total experience, with at least 1 year in a healthcare or hospital supply chain/procurement environment.
Solid grasp of procurement processes, inventory control, vendor management, and healthcare compliance.
Hands-on proficiency with materials management systems, reporting and analytics, and team supervision.
Prior financial oversight or procurement operations experience.
Planning and Organizing – Turning strategy into precise, on-time supply operations
Organizational and Environmental Awareness – Reading hospital needs and market shifts early
Networking and Relationship Building – Earning lasting trust with vendors, clinicians and regulators
Team Leadership – Building leaders and developing successors
Conflict Management – Resolving supplier and stakeholder tension fairly
Stress Management – Staying steady when supply is critical
Communication – Clear, persuasive dealings from the boardroom to the warehouse floor
r: 95% availability of medication and critical hospital supplies
5–10% annual cost savings through supplier negotiation and standardization
15–20% reduction in excess and expired stock through just-in-time and stockless models
>90% on-time, in-full delivery from key suppliers
Strategy & Budgets: Design departmental strategy, own the annual budget, forecast manpower, and drive cost-efficient resource utilization.
Procurement & Contracts: Oversee end-to-end procurement execution, lead major bids, and ensure vendor selection aligns with internal policies.
Inventory & Logistics: Coordinate with stores and pharmacy logistics to monitor consumption trends, manage expiry controls, and drive ERP replenishment.
Supplier Performance: Build vendor relationships, track SLAs, and hold suppliers accountable to contract terms.
Process & Compliance: Enforce standard operating procedures, mitigate supply chain risks, and uphold HSE standards.
Leadership & Succession: Identify successors, manage team performance, and foster cross-functional collaboration with teams.
Achieving timely, cost-effective procurement and end-to-end visibility across the supply chain.
Maintaining effective inventory controls to prevent both stockouts and overstocking.
Ensuring strong vendor compliance, accurate reporting, and proactive risk mitigation.
Fostering smooth team development, defining clear roles, and upholding policy compliance.
